draft.title: Current and voltage
card: Closed circuit
Charge can only flow around a closed circuit, a complete loop with no gaps. A switch that is open makes a gap and the flow stops.
Current
the flow of electric charge around the circuit. It is measured in amperes (amps, A).
Voltage
the push the battery gives the charge. It is measured in volts (V). A higher voltage gives a bigger push.
Symbols
Circuits are drawn with standard symbols so that everyone can read them. A cell or battery, a globe, a switch and connecting wires each have their own symbol.
draft.remember: Current is the flow of charge, in amps. Voltage is the push, in volts.

a.q: Which pair correctly matches each quantity with its unit?
opts: Current in amperes, voltage in volts
Current in volts, voltage in amperes
Current in amperes, voltage in kilograms
Current in volts, voltage in kilograms
a.why: Current is the flow of charge and is measured in amperes. Voltage is the push from the battery and is measured in volts. Swapping the units is tempting, but the flow is in amps and the push is in volts.

b.q: Sam builds a circuit with a battery, a globe and a switch. The globe stays off when the switch is open. What is the best reason?
opts: The open switch leaves a gap, so charge cannot flow
The open switch removes the voltage from the battery
The open switch makes the current flow backwards
The open switch uses up the charge in the wires
b.why: Charge flows only around a closed circuit, and an open switch makes a gap in the loop. The battery still gives a push, but with a gap there is no current. So the globe stays off.
b.clue: Think about what a gap does to a complete loop.
